subject: MAP & closing sprint: AWS private offer + billing path for Gateway Solutions
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@gatewaysolutions.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@gatewaysolutions.com>
Date: 2029-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — MAP draft + AWS private offer questions

Hannah,

Thanks for the call earlier. Maya and I reviewed the draft MAP your team shared on the screen — a couple quick clarifications before we lock dates with procurement: 

- We need the billing cadence spelled out (monthly v. upfront) for the AWS private offer — procurement expects explicit invoice triggers.
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a PO referencing an AWS Marketplace Private Offer (we typically attach the PO to the private offer in the marketplace flow).
- We have an internal security checklist that requires a short section in the MAP about data residency and audit logs (SOC2 evidence link would be ideal).

If you can send an editable MAP (spreadsheet) and an example private-offer invoice path, we can finalize the procurement checklist on our side this week.

Best,
Alex
Gateway Solutions

Attachments: none

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@gatewaysolutions.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@gatewaysolutions.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — MAP draft + AWS private offer questions

Alex / Maya — thanks for the clear list. Putting answers inline and attaching an editable MAP: Gateway_MAP_v3.xlsx.

- Billing cadence: Redwood supports both monthly invoicing and an upfront reservation invoice for Dedicated/Private Offer commitments. For AWS Private Offers we typically route billing through the marketplace seller flow; invoice timing options are captured in tab "Billing Options" in the MAP. Recommended default for initial close: monthly billing with 30-day net terms, then convert to upfront yearly invoice at renewal if you want committed discount pricing.

- PO + Private Offer: yes — we accept a standard PO that references the AWS Marketplace Private Offer ID. The procurement team requires the PO to include the exact private-offer SKU and the HubSpot deal id in the description. The MAP has a checklist item for the PO content under "Procurement".

- Security / audit logs: I've added a short note in the MAP and linked our SOC 2 report in the Drive folder (see related_links). If your team needs an extracted CSV of audit events for a short review window, we can provide a redacted export via secure share.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Your procurement fills the PO template (we will confirm invoice target).
2) We'll exchange PO and Private Offer ID; Redwood legal will do a quick standard acceptance.
3) Kickoff implementation + acceptance sprint (two-week eval window) — see MAP tab "Acceptance & Eval" for proposed dates.

I'm looping Karthik on the billing mechanics and Grace on acceptance checkpoints. Let me know if you'd prefer an executive summary call with procurement on Friday.

Thanks,
Hannah
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Gateway_MAP_v3.xlsx (editable MAP with Billing Options, Acceptance & Eval tabs)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@gatewaysolutions.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@gatewaysolutions.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-24T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — MAP draft + AWS private offer questions

Alex / Maya — quick note on the invoicing path so procurement has the exact steps: 

1) Redwood issues a seller-accepted invoice tied to the AWS Private Offer SKU. Invoice metadata includes the Private Offer ID and the HubSpot deal id.
2) If you select monthly billing, Redwood will create a consolidated monthly invoice; payment via ACH or wire is accepted (payment instructions are in the invoice PDF).
3) For upfront commits: Redwood will issue an upfront invoice at acceptance; we can show a prorated schedule for the first 12 months in the MAP.
4) If procurement requires, we can route the invoice through your cloud reseller (note this may add a 7–10 day delay for reseller processing).

Grace — can you confirm who from CS will own the two-week acceptance sprint and what acceptance criteria we should lock in (sample prompts, latency SLO checks, and a billing smoke test)?

Alex / Maya — attaching the "AWS_Private_Offer_Template.docx" for your legal/procurement team to pre-fill. If procurement wants legal redlines during signature, we can expedite.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: AWS_Private_Offer_Template.docx

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@gatewaysolutions.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@gatewaysolutions.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-07-01T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — MAP draft + AWS private offer questions

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement completed the PO and attached it here (PO_Gateway_332.pdf). A few confirmations from our side so we can schedule the kickoff: 

- We will proceed with monthly billing for the first 90 days and then evaluate switching to an upfront annual commitment at renewal.
- PO references the Private Offer SKU and the HubSpot deal id (as requested).
- Security team reviewed the SOC 2 link and requested a short call next Tuesday to confirm audit log access.

Action items we need from Redwood to close this week:
1) Redwood accepts the PO and returns a seller-accepted invoice or confirmation that the private offer will be created in AWS by the end of this week.
2) Grace to confirm acceptance sprint owner and proposed start date (we prefer 2029-07-08).

Hannah / Karthik — can you confirm acceptance and send the AWS Private Offer ID once it's created? If you accept the PO as-is, procurement is ready to route payment once the private offer is visible in our AWS account.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement | Gateway Solutions

Attachment: PO_Gateway_332.pdf
